# Startup readback: AI-16

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Build repository-owned prompt, model, strict-schema and tool-profile governance for the existing AI runtime. Each run must identify immutable versions for its prompt, selected model policy, output schema and allowed tool profile. Required manager capability cases and hard rules must gate promotion; an unauthorized tool or hard-rule failure must fail closed. A bounded staging golden subset must pass before promoting one candidate, and a later run must prove rollback to the previous version without changing prior run history.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-14 is Done (PR #163, merge `3ce4ecf1`); its `ManagerCode`, `managerCapabilitySchema`, persisted manager capabilities and canonical run/action/evidence contracts define identity and authority. Its completion evidence records passing local contract, DB/RLS, browser and staging create/read/transition proofs. AI-15 is Done (PR #165, merge `b16b4583`); `WorkflowDefinition`, `OperationsManagerRegistry`, `ai-execute`, `prompt_templates.active_version`, `prompt_versions.evaluation_status` and `ai_calls.prompt_version_id` supply the run and persistence path. Its completion evidence records `verify:changed`, exact-candidate staging and bounded real Responses runs through the orchestrator. Keep all privileged promotion behind authenticated/server-owned paths; only the Systems workflow currently allowlists `review_prompt_promotion`.

## Implementation and boundaries

Extend `packages/ai-runtime/src/eval.ts` and its current `eval.test.ts` / `manager-evals.test.ts` into repository-owned, per-manager cases for evidence, prohibited behavior, tool authority, cost/latency and cross-manager boundaries. Connect versioned prompt/schema/tool policy and the model route to the persisted `prompt_versions` / `ai_calls` path and `supabase/functions/ai-execute/index.ts`; enforce immutable candidate versions, strict output validation, promotion thresholds, and an explicit rollback path. `execution-policy.ts` already fails closed for unknown workflows and model IDs, but the Responses request currently sends `tools: []`; define bounded profiles without adding arbitrary execution. Keep the run/version fields required here in existing run/AI-call records and avoid changing AI-19's general trace/audit ownership. Do not replace AI-14 contracts, weaken server authorization or hard budgets, rely on an external black-box eval service, run the exhaustive matrix against paid models, or add manager business logic. Any prompt-governance status or action shown to users must preserve the Frontend Constitution's evidence and uncertainty states; avoid a general Operations dashboard redesign.

## Local tests and commands

Use deterministic fixtures as the inner loop: `corepack pnpm --filter @ai-operations/ai-runtime test` for golden/capability evaluation cases, `corepack pnpm exec deno test supabase/functions/ai-execute/execution-policy.test.ts` for workflow/model/action allowlists, plus focused migration/contract coverage for immutable versions and promotion/rollback invariants. Then run `corepack pnpm verify:changed` as the required final local proof; its impact routing should select the changed package, Edge and database checks. Keep model/provider mocks on the same reservation, validation, run and trace paths as the live call.

## Hosted proof and readiness

Live proof is required only at the Responses provider boundary: run one to three representative staging golden cases through the canonical orchestrator, using safe synthetic fixtures, the lowest-cost permitted route and the configured hard ceiling. Confirm the candidate's prompt/model/schema/tool-policy version references in the accepted run, promote it, then make one subsequent run after rollback and verify the earlier run history is unchanged. AI-15 already proved the staged Responses path, and its evidence says AI-65 verified staging/production credential mapping; recheck current staging readiness, fixture identity/reset, permission grants and acceptance-evidence producer/validator/consumer wiring before dispatch. Do not spend on the full matrix or proceed if budget, validation, version trace or evidence disagrees.

## Delegation and blockers

Use one coding owner through merge; no subagents or review panels are needed for this bounded runtime/governance surface. AI-19 has a separate active worktree at the same `origin/main` base and owns general trace/audit/correlation work, so coordinate any shared trace-contract change and keep this ticket's edits to prompt/model/schema/tool version references needed for governance. If staging credentials, provider access or required operator MFA is unavailable, park only that hosted proof with the precise failed check and resume command; continue local work and preserve the existing auth, budget, staging and production-release controls.

## Remaining-work readback · 2026-10-20

The exact deployed candidate `bd08c784212cde43de864ed07f72c1cb3855eff8` (tree `5d1edd7f100b646428d765278ef9f0d1e6389a79`, staging deployment run `39420252332`) reached the password form, but sign-in timed out after 300 seconds at `/login` while Playwright waited for `POST /api/auth/sign-in` navigation. No MFA or protected acceptance operation was reached. That live runner did not capture the response status/body/duration, so the later local root-cause reproduction is a strong match for the stuck navigation but cannot establish the staging POST's actual response.

The local reproduction isolated the cause: Supabase's isolated local password grant returned HTTP 200 in 93ms and the app POST returned HTTP 303 in under one second, but the response Location used `http://localhost:<port>/mfa` while the configured public origin and browser used `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Chromium blocked the cross-origin `/mfa` request under CSP (`requestfailed=csp`). Hosted Wrangler and deploy configuration set the exact staging/production `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN`.

The route now binds login and MFA redirects to `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` (falling back to the request URL only when that setting is absent). Route tests cover a framework/internal request host that differs from the public origin. Credential-bearing browser tests disable Playwright tracing and report only status, path, origin, elapsed time, and safe network failure codes.

**Production-runtime local evidence after the fix:** OpenNext Cloudflare build passed under Linux/WSL. Wrangler ran the built Worker with `--local`; its bindings were reported local, including local Supabase, R2 and Worker self-reference. The login page returned 200 with zero browser console errors. The direct sign-in route and native Chromium form both reached the same-origin `/mfa` challenge (2/2 tests passed) using the synthetic local Supabase account. No staging or provider resources were used.

**Final local gate:** `corepack pnpm verify:changed` passed all 9 selected profiles: formatting, lint, typecheck, workspace tests, infrastructure tests, web build, DB/backfill, Edge checks and Chromium. DB verification applied the migrations and passed 467 pgTAP assertions; Chromium passed 17/17. The first gate run exposed a Windows-only CRLF assumption in the agent-native skills metadata test; the assertion now accepts LF and CRLF, the narrow repro passed 2/2, and the complete gate passed on rerun. Existing web lint emitted 10 warnings and Next.js emitted its middleware deprecation notice; no errors remained.

**Still required:** update PR #170 with this fix, wait for exact-head CI/security, deploy the new immutable candidate, then perform only AI-16's bounded real-Responses candidate/promotion/rollback acceptance. AI-19's representative hosted correlation proof remains separate and must run against its own exact candidate. Do not spend another staging login until the new candidate's CI and deployment identity are verified.

### Remaining-work evidence — 20 Oct 2026

The current staging 500 remains recorded in Linear on both AI-16 and AI-19. It occurred on the old exact candidate `c7a8be07bb48590cf724c6c7aeea2bd7b8261487`, deployment run `39442814542`, at `/mfa?job=schedule_update&returnTo=%2Foverview` (React #441, digest `2096031138@E1180`, Cloudflare Ray `a4d8da725c6f6515-LHR`). Root cause is now confirmed locally: session refresh began during Server Component rendering, then the SSR cookie adapter attempted a forbidden cookie write.

The AI-16 worktree now refreshes the Supabase session in middleware before rendering, forwards rotated cookies into the current request and response, and prevents caching refreshed responses. - `corepack pnpm verify:changed`: 10/10 selected checks pass, including DB/backfill, Edge, Chromium 17/17, the Worker regression and dependency audit.
- Generated `apps/web/next-env.d.ts` build changes were restored. PR #170 had pushed head `36fdcffcb2d68bba5e08d1c02af1ab635fedf332`; no newer middleware-fix candidate has been deployed to staging.

**CI boundary failure and local parity correction:** PR #170 head `36fdcffcb2d68bba5e08d1c02af1ab635fedf332` passed core, CodeQL, security and dependency review. CI run `39453100796`, boundary job `118732822107`, passed DB/backfill, Edge checks, Chromium 17/17 and dependency audit, then the OpenNext Worker MFA E2E failed at server startup with `ENOENT` for `apps/web/.next/server/middleware-manifest.json` while OpenNext loaded the middleware manifest. No staging deployment or sign-in was attempted for this failure.

The local Worker runner had been using WSL Node 24.18.0 while CI and deploy workflows use Node 22.18.0, and it reused a persistent WSL build directory without reinstalling from the frozen lockfile. That made its earlier green Worker run an incomplete CI comparison. The runner now selects and verifies Node 22.18.0 plus pnpm 10.18.2, limits cleanup to the checked disposable WSL copy, removes generated Next/OpenNext/Wrangler output before building, and installs that copy with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. That runtime correction was necessary but did not fully align the environment: the local WSL path did not forward `LOCAL_QA_DIST_DIR`, so its initial green did not exercise the CI failure.

**Exact CI cause reproduced locally:** `run-e2e.ts` sets `LOCAL_QA_DIST_DIR` for the isolated Next build. Playwright builds the webserver environment by merging the parent `process.env` back with `webServer.env`, so deleting the key from a copied object does not remove it. Linux CI therefore sent the non-empty custom dist directory into the Worker preview: Next emitted middleware files under `.next-local-qa-*`, while OpenNext looked under `apps/web/.next`, and startup failed with the same missing `middleware-manifest.json`. The WSL runner had omitted the variable from `WSLENV`, masking the issue. Forcing the variable through the local WSL path reproduced the missing-manifest failure before the fix.

The regression fix clears inherited webserver values with `undefined`, forwards `LOCAL_QA_DIST_DIR` in the Windows WSL test environment so the case remains exercised, and routes both Linux CI and WSL preview startup through `local-worker-preview.sh`. That shared boundary rejects a non-empty leaked override and unsets an empty WSL value before Next builds. The exact forced-variable Worker MFA test now passes 1/1. The complete `corepack pnpm verify:changed` on the fixed worktree passed all 10 selected profiles, including 17/17 Chromium, the OpenNext Worker MFA regression, DB/backfill, Edge checks, web build, typecheck, lint, format and dependency audit. Existing lint and Next/OpenNext dependency warnings were non-fatal. The generated `apps/web/next-env.d.ts` change from the build was restored.

Next: wait for all required CI/security checks on the follow-up exact SHA (especially the Linux Worker preview), and only then deploy that immutable SHA. After deployment identity is verified, run the bounded real-Responses golden subset, candidate promotion and rollback proof. Merge only after hosted acceptance is accepted; finish with the release-pipeline production smoke and Linear evidence.
